newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Japan unfairly blocking fruit imports.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Japan unfairly blocking fruit imports.

text.p: The United States has accused Japan of unreasonably blocking imports of a variety of U.S. apples and other fruit and asked for justification of the action.

In a letter released late Saturday to Japanese Trade Minister Shunpei Tsukahara, Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky, who was in Seattle attending a trade ministers meeting, and Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said discussions on health standards for certain kinds of U.S. apples have been "frustrating and unsuccessful."

The letter said Japan was blocking the imports on the basis of how the apples were treated for codling moth, a common pest whose larva bores into and destroys the fruit, while they accept the same types of apples from New Zealand, where producers use the same treatment methods as those used in the United States.
"We have encountered the same difficulties in seeking access to the Japanese market for new varieties of U.S. cherries and nectarines," the letter added.
The letter asked for Japanese justification for excluding the imports and sought a response no later than Oct. 7.
In January 1995, Japan agreed to import red and golden delicious apples from the United States and U.S. producers have been seeking to export more varieties of the fruit.
